issues.description: The problem statement (part b) requires set_pixel to receive pixel coordinates as 32-bit floats in xmm0 and xmm1 and the color in ECX, but both the provided template and the reference solution implement and invoke set_pixel using integer registers (EAX / EBX) rather than xmm registers. The template's main moves integer coordinates into EAX/EBX and calls set_pixel; the solution's set_pixel reads integers from EAX/EBX. This mismatch will confuse students: they may implement set_pixel expecting floats in xmm0/xmm1 (as the text demands) but the template calls it with integers, or they will implement it for integers while the description asks for floats. Either choice produces a call/argument convention mismatch and blocks correct testing or grading.
issues.suggested_fix:
Make the calling convention consistent across specification, template, and solution. Two options:
1) Update the problem statement to match the template/solution: state that set_pixel receives integer coordinates in EAX (x) and EBX (y) and the RGB color in ECX (as the template and solution currently do). This is the least intrusive fix since both template and solution already follow this convention.
2) Or, if the educational intent is to practice working with SSE float registers, update the template and solution so main passes floats in xmm0/xmm1 (e.g., convert the integer inputs to floats and move them to xmm0/xmm1 before the call) and reimplement set_pixel to consume xmm0/xmm1. Ensure the template's call site, example usage, and the reference solution are updated accordingly.
Either change will remove the argument-register mismatch and prevent student confusion.

issues.description: The problem statement (part b) specifies the set_pixel subroutine interface as receiving pixel coordinates x and y as 32-bit floats in xmm0 and xmm1 and the color in ecx, with the additional constraint that no registers except eax may be modified. The template and the provided solution, however, implement and expect integer coordinates in eax and ebx (see template main TODO comment and the solution's set_pixel/main code). This is an interface/register mismatch for the same conceptual entity (the set_pixel parameter passing convention) and will confuse students: they are asked to implement set_pixel for xmm0/xmm1 but the starter code and reference use eax/ebx and a different register-preservation contract.
issues.suggested_fix:
Make the calling convention consistent across the problem statement, template, and solution. Two practical fixes (pick one):

1) If the exercise should use integer coordinates (minimal change): Update the problem statement (part b) to state that x and y are 32-bit integers passed in EAX and EBX and that ecx holds the RGB value (and adjust the 'only eax may be modified' constraint accordingly). This aligns the textual specification with the template and solution.

2) If the exercise must use float coordinates as specified: Update the template and solution to accept floats in xmm0/xmm1 and implement the conversion and address calculation accordingly (or update the stub and comments). Concretely: implement set_pixel to convert floats to integers (e.g., cvttss2si to get integer x into eax and integer y into another preserved location or onto the stack), compute the byte offset and memory address from display_start, and store ecx to that address; ensure the register-preservation rule in the problem statement is satisfied (or relax it explicitly). 

Either option ensures a single, unambiguous calling convention so students can map the problem requirements to the template and reference solution without extra cognitive overhead.
